<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
## Missing figure: years of experience

The summary gives no years and no dates, so I can't calculate them. **How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** A start year for your earliest relevant role also works.

**If you don't supply it:**
- **You may be filtered out automatically.** "8 years" is a stated requirement. Applicant tracking systems and recruiters often screen on that number first. A summary without it can be rejected or ranked lower before anyone reads about your work.
- **The reader has to guess.** Without a number or dates, a recruiter can't confirm you meet the bar. Many will assume you don't rather than ask.
- **I can't fill it in for you.** I won't invent or imply a figure. The rewrite can only show your level through scope and responsibility, which is weaker evidence than a direct match.

## Draft rewrite (pending your figure)

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building and operating transactional services. Most recently owned a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Prior work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems, with a consistent focus on correctness and reliability in high-volume financial and operational data flows.

**If you have 8 or more years:** I'll put the number first ("8+ years of backend engineering…") so it matches the posting word for word.

**If you have fewer than 8:** I'll state your actual figure and lead with the settlement pipeline's scale to make the case for your fit. I won't blur the number to suggest you meet the requirement.

**If you'd rather not state a number:** Use the draft without the bracketed phrase, knowing the screening risk above. Listing dated roles elsewhere in your résumé would reduce that risk somewhat.
